significance.justification: Verified true, the claim would establish that safety tuning is "sharply shallow" at positions 1–5 and that a measurable alignment-depth profile predicts attack robustness, a form-(iii) predictive coupling supplemented by the causal claim that deepening this profile reduces prefill and mid-sequence bypasses. It establishes both a behavioral phenomenon and a mechanism-level positional account, constraining the expectation that models with flatter, deeper safety profiles should have lower injection attack success rather than merely identifying another refusal direction; this is more specific than the single-direction mechanism studied by Arditi et al. (2024), while Qi et al. (2024, arXiv:2406.05946) shows that token depth is a consequential axis for safety training. True and false are distinguishable, and a negative result—no robust coupling between depth and attack success despite measurable early-token changes—would rule out alignment depth as a general diagnostic or causal training target, although the bundled hypothesis permits mixed outcomes. After topic substitution, generic mechanistic LLM safety would not merit this score; the claim-specific cross-position law and robustness coupling, rather than the topic's importance, support an above-median rating.

reach.justification: The explicit handle is a "mechanistic definition and metric of alignment depth that predicts robustness," also described as a "diagnostic and training target" based on the depth profile. It is potentially ex ante because the profile is claimed to predict robustness before deploying or attacking a tuned model, giving auditors and alignment trainers an opportunity to reject or deepen a shallow model rather than merely explain a completed failure. After per-model re-extraction, the substantive prediction survives as a relation—greater distribution of safety signal across response depth should imply lower prefill and injection success—although the claim acknowledges possible dependence on alignment recipe and does not clearly assert transfer across architectures, scales, or modalities. The topic-substitution check lowers no score here: generic safety interpretability supplies neither this forward-looking depth metric nor its training constraint, but the uncertain breadth of the asserted scope keeps it from the highest reach bands.
